headline: 芭蕾活到老與獨立影院的復甦
context: 藝文版今天有兩則輕快的故事。一位倫敦女士從小愛上芭蕾，八十多歲仍靠舞蹈保持活力。大西洋另一邊，美國各地的獨立電影院悄悄回春，以精選片單和社群感挑戰連鎖影城。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: The first time I saw a show, I felt like I had discovered a new language. It’s since become one of my greatest pleasures When I was a young girl living in suburban London in the early 1960s, I was looking for ways to find excitement. The first time my mother took me to see the London Festival Ballet (now the English National Ballet), I felt a sense of rapture as I realised that the body could say things words could not. I was yearning for more, and that night at the Royal Festival Hall, I saw glimmers of the world out there waiting for me. Watching the dancers, I felt something shift in me. It was like discovering a new language, one that I immediately wanted to speak. Continue reading...
sources.title: I fell in love with ballet as a young girl – now it’s keeping me active in my eighties

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: With unexpected programming and a community ethos, independent cinemas across the US are giving multiplexes a run for their money On a quiet street in New York City’s Ridgewood neighborhood stands an unassuming, windowless white building. Its lone door, covered with an amalgamation of cut-outs, looks like a teenager’s bedroom; the building numbers are displayed via peeling stickers above it. But if you look closely, herein lies Low Cinema, an indie movie theater which boasts just 42 seats and thrives on being lo-fi. “We need to bring back theaters that are the size of porno theaters but don’t necessarily play pornographic films,” cracks owner John Wilson , who is best known as the host of HBO Max’s popular How To with John Wilson and opened Low Cinema in spring 2025. Continue reading...
sources.title: ‘There’s excitement in the air’: how America fell back in love with indie cinemas

thread_text:
芭蕾活到老與獨立影院的復甦

倫敦有位女士，1960 年代在郊區第一次看了芭蕾表演，從此愛上舞蹈。她現在八十多歲，仍靠芭蕾保持活力，說那是她發現的「新語言」。大西洋另一邊，美國各地的獨立電影院正在悄悄回春。小型社區影院以精選片單和社群氛圍，與連鎖影城一較高下。

—— 本則來自《衛報》，2026 年 7 月 4 日發佈，讓圖書館員翻譯給你聽。
threads_text:
倫敦有位女士，1960 年代在郊區第一次看了芭蕾表演後，從此愛上舞蹈。她現在八十多歲，說芭蕾是讓她一直保持活力的東西。大西洋另一邊，美國各地獨立電影院正悄悄回春，以精選片單和社群氛圍與連鎖影城競爭，吸引觀眾重新回流。

本則整理自《衛報》於 2026 年 7 月 4 日發佈的報導。
voice_text: 兩則今天的藝文輕快小事。倫敦有位女士，1960 年代在郊區第一次看了芭蕾，從此再沒放下。她現在八十多歲，說舞蹈是讓她一直保持活力的東西。另一頭，美國的獨立電影院這幾年悄悄回春。小型社區影院以精選片單和社群感，讓觀眾重新回流，跟連鎖影城搶生意。
